_comment: The rule inventory (feature 015, FR-001). One entry per distinct failure-emission site in
a grading script. 'emitAnchor' is a literal substring of the message as it appears in the
script source — it is how Coverage.Tests.ps1 ties an inventory entry to the line that
emits it, so a rule that is deleted or reworded is caught rather than silently orphaned.
Phase 1 inventories Invoke-StructureCheck only; phase 2 adds the two GAP rules it closes; phases 3 and 4 complete it.
DIRECTIONS. Every rule has a 'fail' case and a 'pass' case, and from T029 on those names
mean 'the condition the rule names HOLDS' and 'the nearest state in which it does not'.
For the adverse rules — the great majority — that is the same thing as failing and
passing. It is not for the inert and affirmative verdicts scope-check-repos.ps1 emits: a
'fail' case for 'n/a (declared but not present here)' exits 0, because the rule under test
IS the n/a. Naming those directions after the exit code would have meant leaving the inert
verdicts out of the inventory, and the inert verdicts are precisely what SC-004 and GAP-027
are about — a state in which nothing was graded must not read as a graded pass.
EXEMPTIONS (FR-004, added in phase 6). A rule MAY carry an 'exemption' field instead of a
pass/fail pair. The field is the written reason, it is printed on every run, and the rule
stays in the inventory so the site cannot be reworded or deleted unnoticed. An exemption is
not 'not yet covered': it is a stated position that a faithful fixture cannot be built, and
every one of them says what would be needed instead.
ANCHOR FILE (feature 018). A rule MAY carry an 'anchorFile': a file under scripts/ that is not the
script the case runs. It is for a message emitted by a shared library the script calls (the
reader of codeRepos moved from scripts/scope-check-repos.ps1 into scripts/adoption-lib.ps1 when
a second script needed it). The rule is still graded by running the script; only where its
anchor is searched changes, and the anchor must name exactly siteCount non-comment lines of that file.

rules.summary: a digest on disk does not match what its sources produce
rules.law: CLAUDE.md Task-Scoped Reading (a digest is never a source-of-truth rung, so it may never drift from the law it digests)
rules.notes: The pass direction over this recipe is the GAP-025 demonstration: a '<!--' inside an inline code span opened a phantom comment that swallowed every later marker, so a CORRECT digest was reported stale and a regenerated one silently lost rules. Feature 016 adds three directions for GAP-028, where a code span wraps across the lines of its paragraph: 'pass-wrapped-span' (the correct digest reported stale by per-line reading) and 'fail-wrapped-span' (a stale digest missing that rule, which per-line reading called fresh - the fail-open direction), both green-turning; and 'pass-comment-block-backticks', a guard that failed under the first fix's cross-block pairing (016 FR-007, plan D7). A fourth, 'pass-tail-after-close', is round-1 review F2's second document: a comment closes mid-line and the line then quotes the opener in a span; 7a770e5 and 6f75415 lost the next marker, and plan D10 (an opener disarmed only when it cannot be a comment) harvests it. Five more are guards for D10's model, each a marker inside a real comment that must not be harvested, with a correct digest on disk (016 plan D11): 'pass-hidden-nbsp-line' (a no-break-space line is not blank - mutation g), 'pass-hidden-pre-under-tag-line' and 'pass-hidden-pre-in-misread-fence' (a pre block a tag line or a misread fence would mask - mutation h), 'pass-hidden-html-block-open' (raw HTML - mutation f) and 'pass-hidden-after-backslash-spans' (the closer check - mutation e); the first three harvested the marker on 8e45e37. Ten more come from the round-4 review (016 T014m), each a marker inside raw HTML that must not be harvested: 'pass-hidden-div-after-comment-line' and 'pass-hidden-div-after-pre' (the enclosing div resumes when an inner block closes - mutation i), 'pass-hidden-div-in-misread-fence' (a blank-ending block start on a fenced line - mutation j), 'pass-hidden-list-div' and 'pass-hidden-quote-div' (container markers - mutations k and k2), 'pass-hidden-comment-block-open', 'pass-hidden-pi-block', 'pass-hidden-cdata-block' and 'pass-hidden-declaration-block' (each long end - mutations l1-l4), and 'pass-hidden-script-after-tag' (a raw-text element opened later on a tag line - mutation m); the first three and the last harvested the marker on b45cff1. Since 016 phase 2 (plan D8 and D11 as amended during phase 2) each of the 22 pass-hidden-* guards (those named above and the ones later review rounds added) also expects DIGEST-020's skipped-marker report naming its hidden marker, and exit 1: the marker is still not harvested, and a mutation that harvests it drops the report and reads the digest stale.

rules.summary: a Critical feature that is provably mid-feature is warned that its independence artifact is pending, and not failed for it
rules.law: docs/sdlc/definition-of-done.md item 6 (the human review is once per feature, at merge); feature 024 spec FR-001, FR-002

rules.notes: GAP-022. Two emission sites, declared: the team arm names human-pr-review.md and the solo arm names second-model-review.md, and both say the same thing - which artifact is owed once the final phase lands. Mid-feature means tasks.md declares phases 1..N with no gap and the branch carries a phase commit below N and none at N. The pass is the WARN with exit 0; the fail is the same branch once the final phase commit lands, where today's failure is back unchanged. Variants: the solo arm (the cooling-off is not demanded while mid-feature either), and a final phase heading that exists only inside a fenced block, which declares nothing. The parent exits 1 on every pass here.

rules.notes: One site, several reasons, each a variant: no phase heading in tasks.md (the fail), a gap in the heading numbers (so an invented high phase cannot hold a branch in WARN), no phase commit yet, and a depth-1 clone with no diff base. The failure itself is the unchanged CriticalEvidence message; what is new is the WARNING line naming the reason, so a branch held strict is never quiet about it. Recorded in 024's notes: the plan named six rules (CRIT-R01 to CRIT-R06) and the coverage sweep owns one rule per emission site, of which there are two, so the six conditions became variants of these two.

rules.summary: a Critical feature whose plan declares Merge Readiness: pending is warned that its independence artifact is deferred, whatever the subjects, headings or history say
rules.law: docs/sdlc/definition-of-done.md item 6 (the human review is once per feature, at merge); feature 025 spec FR-001, FR-002, FR-003
rules.notes: GAP-022 follow-up. Two emission sites, declared: the team arm names human-pr-review.md and the solo arm names second-model-review.md. The pass is the owner's declared pending on a branch shaped like FitForge 002 (duplicate 'Phase N amendment' headings, 'tasks: phase N done' subjects, the final phase landing before phase 2), where feature 024 reads final-landed and fails; the fail is the same branch with ready, today's failure. Variants: the solo arm; a depth-1 clone and a tasks.md with no phase heading (an explicit declaration needs no history, plan D2; a missing tasks.md cannot be used, the Structure check fails it first); a committed invalid artifact (pending never suppresses the arm's grading); a marker inside a one-line comment, a multi-line comment, a fence or a code span (hidden, so feature 024 decides), and a visible pending with a trailing comment (the comment is stripped, the value reads exactly pending); a Standard feature carrying the marker (ignored, plan D4). rules.summary: a commit amends an approved feature document with no conforming approver record
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority (you never approve your own amendment)
rules.emitAnchor: after approval with no conforming approver record
rules.notes: Forty-five directions (the count that stood at twenty-two had been stale since feature 025 added three; feature 026 adds twenty), because the rule is mostly made of what it does NOT fire on. Four fail: 'fail' (no record), 'fail-hidden-record' (a correct record inside an unterminated HTML comment - H1), 'fail-placeholder' (an unfilled slot, which prints what it rejected - D6), 'fail-rename-content' (a contract renamed and reinterpreted in one commit - H3). Six pass: 'pass' (a conforming record) and the exemptions - creation (D2), a ticked checkbox (D3c), Draft to Approved (D3d), a renumbered feature directory (J3), and 'pass-rename-identical', the sibling of 'fail-rename-content' that pins a byte-identical move as no amendment at all. Two more cover git reality (T026): 'fail-nonascii' (core.quotepath) and 'pass-merge' (a second parent, D7). Every fixture commits a stub scripts/enforcement-pack.ps1 defining this function, because the D2b boundary asks the parent tree whether the check existed - without it every commit reports as pre-boundary and the fixture grades nothing while printing green. Feature 016 adds three for GAP-028 (a code span that wraps within its paragraph): 'fail-wrapped-span-hidden', which pins a known limitation - a visible record after a wrapped span stays hidden, because this check keeps the per-line reading on purpose (016 plan D11, spec US2 as amended; 014 B7's shape, fail-closed; the case was 'pass-wrapped-span' until three review rounds found every other reading let some hidden record count); and two guards that fail under an over-reaching fix, 'fail-hidden-after-unpaired' (no-fail-open: a record inside a real comment stays hidden when unpaired backticks surround it - 016 FR-006, 014 H1's shape) and 'pass-comment-block-backticks' (a record after an HTML comment block whose lines hold backticks stays visible - 016 FR-007). The phase-1 review (F1) added three more fail directions, each a record inside a real comment that a backtick misread would disarm - 'fail-hidden-backslash-closer' (spans ending in a backslash, where escapes do not apply), 'fail-hidden-autolink-backtick' (an autolink's backtick, which delimits nothing) and 'fail-hidden-pre-block' (a pre block across a blank line, which runs to its closing tag); each passed on 7a770e5. The round-2 review added four: 'fail-hidden-list-div', 'fail-hidden-list-pre' (raw HTML blocks opened inside a list item) and 'fail-hidden-comment-tick' (a backtick inside an inline comment shifting the pairing), each passing on 6f75415; and 'fail-hidden-html-block-open', a guard where a comment opened inside raw HTML stays open across a blank line. Each of these failed on a 016 design that changed this check's reading; under 016 plan D11 the check keeps the parent's per-line reading, and they stand as the no-fail-open guards any future change to it must pass. Feature 026 (a merge commit that authors content is graded, plan D1-D5) adds twenty merge variants. Six are controls that pass on the parent commit by design, because the merge authored nothing and its output is byte-identical: pass-merge-main-into-branch (shaped like the kit's real Merge branch main into NNN), pass-merge-conflict-take-branch-side and pass-merge-conflict-take-side-whole (a comparison against the first parent alone would wrongly grade the second), pass-merge-clean-automatic (git's own automatic merge of two amended parents, D2), pass-merge-tick-only-both-parents and pass-merge-status-only (the exemptions held against every parent, D3). The rest fail on the parent commit and pair with them: fail-merge-octopus-clean-combination (the same clean combination with a third parent, graded by the fail-closed fallback) with pass-merge-octopus-record; feature 025's reproduction, fail-merge-readiness-added-in-merge-unapproved with pass-merge-readiness-added-in-merge-approved (SC-002); fail-merge-hand-merged-conflict with pass-merge-hand-merged-conflict-record, and fail-merge-combines-approved-amendments (a record is new only against every parent, D4); fail-merge-octopus-authors-plan; fail-merge-tick-vs-rewrite and fail-merge-status-plus-text (an exemption that fails against one parent grades the merge, D3); fail-merge-deletes-approved-document (both parents carry the contract); the usual main-into-branch shapes the phase 2 review found fail-open, fail-merge-deletes-contract-main-into-branch and fail-merge-renames-and-rewrites-contract (main never held the feature directory, so absence in that parent is not equality with it); and fail-merge-record-with-inline-comment (the record pattern is read from the raw line, as an ordinary commit reads it). The failure text is this rule's own with one clause appended for a merge. Feature 027 (a commit that amends ANOTHER feature's approved document is graded, plan D1-D5; sixty-six directions at the end of phase 1, eighty-two with phase 2's Lite lane) adds twenty-one. Twelve fail on the parent commit, which graded only specs/<branch>/ and printed OK: fail-other-feature-no-record (the shape feature 026's phase 3 review reproduced), fail-other-feature-contract, fail-other-feature-record-in-own-notes and fail-other-feature-record-in-own-plan (a record elsewhere approves nothing: one conforming record per amended document of another feature, spec FR-005), fail-other-feature-two-docs-one-record, fail-other-and-own-no-record (the failure names both files and the clause names the other feature only), fail-other-feature-tick-with-rewrite (the tick exemption is for the checkbox alone), fail-other-feature-single-doc-moved (not a renumbering: the old directory still holds documents, so the old path is graded as a removal), fail-other-feature-removal (the owner's sub-decision: a removal has no passing path), fail-other-feature-doc-moved-in (the review F1 shape: one document of an approved feature renamed INTO the branch's own directory is the same removal, and used to print OK), and the two merges fail-merge-other-feature-hand-merged and fail-merge-other-feature-deletes-contract (026's authored-content rule, widened to every feature). Nine pass. Eight pass on the parent too, by design (the record is there, nothing is amended, or the document was never approved at the diff base): pass-other-feature-record (the twin of the first fail), pass-other-feature-created-on-branch (absent at the base, plan D2) and its merge arm pass-merge-other-feature-created-on-branch (a merge rewrites a document this branch created: equal to neither parent, but never approved at the base, plan D4), pass-other-feature-tick, pass-other-feature-status-only, pass-other-feature-renumber-whole-dir (D3 step 4), pass-other-feature-sole-doc-moved-in (the control of fail-other-feature-doc-moved-in: the old directory holds no other graded document, so nothing is removed), pass-merge-other-feature-main-into-branch (shaped like the kit's real merges, output byte-identical). The ninth, the merge twin pass-merge-other-feature-hand-merged-record, passes on the parent with a different roll-up line (the parent skips the merge, this rule grades it). Feature 027 phase 2 (the Lite lane, plan D6, D9) adds sixteen more, on docs/x, fix/x and chore/x, each a branch with no feature directory of its own. Nine fail on the parent, which graded nothing on a Lite branch and printed OK with exit 0: fail-lite-docs-no-record, fail-lite-fix-no-record and fail-lite-chore-no-record (an approved plan of another feature amended with no record), fail-lite-docs-removal (a contract removed, no passing path), fail-lite-docs-moved-off-specs (an approved plan moved to a path outside specs/, which git reports by its new path only: the gate reads the diff again without rename detection) fail-lite-merge-hand-merged-no-record (a merge on a docs/ branch hand-resolves another feature's plan with no record: graded as the merge authoring the change, the 026 rule widened) and their four record twins pass-lite-docs-record, pass-lite-fix-record, pass-lite-chore-record and pass-lite-merge-hand-merged-record (whose roll-up line can only come from the merge, because the branch's other commit touches no approved document), whose roll-up line is new. Six are controls whose output is the parent's, byte for byte: pass-lite-docs-moved-non-spec (the same rename shape for a file that is not a spec document), pass-lite-docs-readme-only (README.md and the roadmap only, the docs/ lane line unchanged), its depth-1 clone pass-lite-docs-readme-only-shallow (no base and no spec document, so the check stays silent, spec FR-009), pass-lite-docs-claim-creation (a docs/claim-* branch that adds a feature directory and edits it in a second commit: not at the base), pass-lite-fix-creation-only (a creation is not an amendment), and fail-lite-fix-contract-refused-first (a contract of another feature changed on a fix/ branch WITH a record: the amendment check passes it and LiteAndAbuse refuses the path first and alone, the plan D6 order; it prints the roll-up line, which is new, and the same single failure as before). On a Lite branch the failure text names the amended file and the feature it belongs to and carries no clause about an own directory, because there is none.

Feature 027 adds pass-other-feature and fail-other-feature: the same pair for an amendment of ANOTHER feature's document, the failure carrying the clause that names the file's feature.

rules.summary: the boundary cannot be computed because the clone is shallow

rules.emitAnchor: this is a shallow clone, so the boundary
rules.notes: Asked of git directly ('rev-parse --is-shallow-repository') rather than inferred from the base, because a shallow clone can still resolve origin/main - a base that looks fine says nothing about whether the history behind it is present. Phase 4 review F1: this used to return bare, printing nothing and exiting 0, which is indistinguishable from a branch that is legitimately pre-boundary.

rules.summary: there is no integration branch to compute a range against
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority; FR-011

rules.summary: a commit's parent cannot be read, so whether it predates the check is unknown

rules.notes: Built with 'truncateBlob': an object that is in the store and cannot be inflated. This is the damage mode review G1 measured - 'cat-file -e' and 'cat-file -s' both report it fine, and only reading the body fails where a reader fails. rules.summary: a run with no computable base says that nothing was compared
rules.law: FR-009 (the Lite lane must not newly fail on a null base) and FR-011; GAP-027
rules.emitAnchor: enforcement-pack: no integration branch to diff against, so nothing on '$Branch' was compared
rules.notes: GAP-027's own line. Both directions exit 0 - what differs is whether the run admits it compared nothing - so the fail direction is the shape the roadmap describes: a fix/ branch on a baseless clone, green, having graded nothing. Phase 5 (T039-T041) gives this an UNGRADED verdict state; when it rewords this line the stale-anchor assertion will say so, which is the point of inventorying it now rather than after. Feature 035: the anchor names the no-integration-branch wording only; when git could not read the base (merge-base exit other than 0 or 1) the same site prints a different sentence, owned by BASE-001.

rules.summary: a branch whose name matches no lane is failed on the name, not passed on the silence

rules.notes: The last arm of the dispatch chain, and the one that decides what an unrecognised name means. 'feature/thing' reaches no lane at all, so every scripted check is skipped: without this rule the run would be indistinguishable from a clean one. Pass and fail differ only in the branch name (plan D10) - 'chore/thing' over the identical tree.

rules.summary: a table in a governance document is severed by a blank or comment line, has a delimiter row with no header, or has a row whose cell count differs from its header; or a list is split by a comment line at column zero

rules.notes: One site, three conditions, because the scanner (Get-StructureFindings in markdown-lib.ps1) returns findings and doc-lint accumulates them in one place, the way $broken holds every unresolved reference. The 'fail' fixture is the recorded defect, a digest-marker-shaped comment between two rows; its variants (blank line, multi-line comment, delimiter separated from its header, header and delimiter disagreeing, an extra or a missing cell) each break the 'pass' table in exactly one way, and the pass variants are the legal near-misses: a marker after the table, an escaped pipe, two adjacent tables, a fence of either kind, a row indented four spaces, prose that starts with a pipe, a table ending the file with no newline, CRLF. The list rule (feature 020 phase 2) reports through the same accumulator, so its variants live here too: a comment at column zero between two items, with and without blank lines around it, as the failing pair; and as the passing near-misses a loose list, a marker after the last item, a comment indented into an item, a parenthesis-numbered list, a fence, a spaced thematic break, and two lists a paragraph apart. Absence is information and never a finding (FR-005, FR-013): an adoption predating feature 017 declares nothing and is simply not armed, so the fail direction is the list not being usable as a floor and the armed line simply does not appear, the way VK-018's fail direction is the field's absence. rules.notes: The check cannot arm on a list it cannot read in full, so it reports UNGRADED (phase 3); the doctor is the half that tells the project why its floor is not there. Seven failing directions, each a different way for a declaration to be unusable: 'fail' (a non-array), 'fail-null', 'fail-blank-entry', 'fail-non-string', and three that would otherwise sit in the list looking like coverage and match nothing, a hole in the floor - 'fail-absolute-path', 'fail-drive-letter' and 'fail-dotdot'. The drive-letter and dotdot cases exist because deleting those alternatives from the reader's pattern passes every other case. A problem never makes the result MORE armed than the same record without it, and an unusable entry is never silently dropped from an otherwise armed list.

rules.summary: a Standard or Micro feature whose Territory reaches a declared critical surface fails
rules.law: feature 017 FR-006, FR-007, FR-011; constitution X (Level declaration)
rules.emitAnchor: but its Territory reaches critical surface
rules.notes: The point of the feature: the declared level was the one decision that selects every other rule's rigour and nothing graded it. Seven directions. 'fail' is a literal file under a surface; 'fail-glob-prefix' is a Territory glob broader than the surface (src/** against src/auth/), which a literal-only reading would let through; 'fail-micro' reads the feature-global block in spec.md; 'fail-multirepo' is the nested layout, Territory and surface both repo-prefixed (feature 012), so one matcher serves a path inside a code repository as it serves one in the governance repository; 'fail-case-and-slash' pins that case is folded and a backslash reads as a slash, the same on every runner. 'pass' is armed, graded, clean. 'pass-critical' pins FR-011: the same Territory on a Critical feature adds no LevelSurface failure - the only failure there is the Critical lane's own missing second-model review. The prefix rule over-reports by design (two overlapping-prefix patterns are called intersecting even when their globs are disjoint): a false positive costs one written exception, a false negative costs the point of the rule.

rules.summary: a project that declares no critical surfaces sees one informational line and no change of verdict
rules.law: feature 017 FR-005, SC-004; constitution X (Level declaration)
rules.notes: Absence is information, never a failure and never UNGRADED: an adoption that predates feature 017 declares nothing, and updating the kit must not turn it red or change its verdict. The line exists so the absence is audible rather than a quiet pass. The fail direction is the line NOT appearing, because a usable list arms the floor and the run grades instead (the way VK-018's fail direction is an absence). An explicit empty list is lawful and reads the same.

rules.summary: a criticalSurfaces declaration that is unusable or whose record cannot be read leaves the run UNGRADED, by name
rules.law: feature 017 FR-012; feature 015 D6 (UNGRADED never changes the exit code)
rules.emitAnchor: LevelSurface: criticalSurfaces in kit-adoption.json is unusable
rules.notes: Two sites, one rule: the list is malformed ('fail', a string where an array belongs), or the record itself exists and cannot be read ('fail-unreadable', JSON that does not parse). The second is deliberately NOT the same as a project that never asked: the check cannot know whether a floor was declared, so it says so by name (spec FR-012, phase 2 review F2) instead of reporting an unarmed pass. UNGRADED exits 0, on the record, because feature 014's FR-009 forbids a new hard failure on the Lite lane; the doctor reports the malformed list as a finding (VK-030).

rules.summary: an armed floor with no readable Territory to grade is UNGRADED, never a pass
rules.law: feature 017 FR-012; research R3
rules.notes: A spec-only branch has no Territory yet (it is written in tasks.md, after the spec is approved), so the floor cannot run and must not look clean. 'fail' is Standard with no tasks.md; 'fail-near-miss' is a **Territory** marker with no colon, the shape the parser reports rather than guesses at. The Structure check independently fails a missing tasks.md; the two findings are separate.

rules.summary: an approved Surface Exception for the exact reaching path passes that path and is listed in the run
rules.law: feature 017 FR-009, US4; constitution X (Level declaration), constitution I
rules.notes: The way an honest feature passes (GAP-020's lesson: a check with no legitimate way to pass trains people to route around it). Listed, not silent: a reader of the run sees what was excepted and why. The approval is validated by the amendment check's own function, so what counts as a well-formed approver has one definition. The self-approval prohibition is held by review alone, as in constitution I.

rules.summary: an exception that names no Territory entry reaching a surface is reported as stale and never fails
rules.law: feature 017 FR-010
rules.notes: The Territory narrowed, or the path was never on a surface. Left in a spec the exception would read as protection it no longer gives, so it is named; it is not failed, because a stale line is housekeeping rather than a violation.

rules.summary: an exception without a conforming approval does not count, and the run says why
rules.law: feature 017 FR-009; constitution I (Amendment authority)
rules.notes: Fires in addition to the reaching-path failure, never instead of it: 'fail' has no approval line, 'fail-placeholder-approver' has an unfilled name (feature 014's D6, same function). 'fail-wrong-path' pins that an approved exception naming a DIFFERENT path covers nothing: the reaching path still fails and the exception is reported stale. 'pass' is a conforming approval.

rules.summary: a spec carrying the Rationale Rule marker has no Level Rationale section
rules.law: feature 017 FR-002, FR-008; constitution X (Level declaration)
rules.notes: The written half of the level claim. The marker is the promise that the section exists, so its absence is the failure ('fail'). 'pass-no-marker' pins FR-008: a spec from before the rule is exempt, silent, and the run is what it was before this feature - without that exemption every shipped feature and every adopted project's history would fail. 'pass-template-marker' is the marker exactly as the spec template writes it, a trailing space and a multi-line comment: the reader must see the line the author sees (phase 1 review F3). A spec can omit the marker and so stand outside the rule; the constitution states that evasion rather than hiding it.

rules.summary: a trigger is left unanswered: absent, with no reason, with a bad verdict, left as the template placeholder, or answered twice
rules.law: feature 017 FR-002; docs/sdlc/critical-delivery.md (the four triggers)
rules.notes: One finding per unanswered trigger, so an unedited template names all four. Each of the four keys has its own direction (fail, fail-missing-irreversible-data, fail-missing-authn-authz-payment, fail-missing-auditable-evidence), so a reader that stopped after three or matched keys loosely would pass one of them. 'fail-no-reason' and 'fail-bad-verdict' pin that a verdict needs its reason. 'fail-template-placeholder' pins phase 1 review F3: text that starts with [ is unfilled, so the template as shipped can never read as four answers. 'fail-duplicate' pins that the first of two answers does not silently win over the second.

rules.summary: the declared level contradicts the answers: Standard with a trigger that applies, or Critical with nothing applying and no reason
rules.law: feature 017 FR-003; constitution X (Level declaration)
rules.notes: Two sites, one rule: the claim and the level disagree in either direction. Over-declaring is lawful ('pass-critical-because'), but it must be said why, or the level is the unexplained choice this feature exists to make explicit; a Critical because line left as the template's bracketed placeholder is not a reason ('fail-critical-because-placeholder'). The Critical cases also fail the Critical lane's own missing second-model review, independently; the case pins that LevelRationale adds only its own finding.

rules.summary: a Rationale Rule marker this check cannot read - an unknown value anywhere, or a line that looks like the marker but is not one - leaves the rationale UNGRADED
rules.law: feature 017 FR-012; feature 015 D6
rules.emitAnchor: the Level Rationale was not checked
rules.notes: Two sites, one rule. A spec from a newer rule version must not be silently exempt, nor graded by rules it was not written for ('fail'), and with two marker lines the ORDER must not decide the verdict ('fail-two-markers' and 'fail-two-markers-reversed' say the same thing). A line that merely LOOKS like the marker - indented, quoted, a space before the colon - is not 'no marker': that would silently exempt a spec that tried to opt in, so it is UNGRADED by name ('fail-near-miss-marker', 'fail-near-miss-spaced-colon'), the way a Territory marker the parser cannot read already is (phase 4 review F3, F4). UNGRADED exits 0, on the record, like every other member that forms no opinion.

rules.summary: there is no origin remote, so there is no claim ledger
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.emitAnchor: 'roadmap-claims: n/a (no origin remote — no claim ledger to check against)'
rules.notes: Declining OUT LOUD is the requirement: a silent exit 0 here is indistinguishable from a roadmap that is actually honest.

rules.summary: origin is configured and cannot be reached
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.emitAnchor: 'roadmap-claims: n/a (origin unreachable — cannot read the claim ledger)'
rules.notes: Kept distinct from having no remote at all: one is a state of the project, the other a state of the machine, and the reader needs different things from each.

rules.summary: the ledger holds no numbered claims
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.notes: An OK rather than an n/a: the ledger WAS read and it is empty, which is a verdict rather than a declined one.

rules.summary: the tree has no docs/roadmap.md
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.notes: An adopter roadmap is adopter-authored and may not exist. The check declines rather than manufacturing a failure out of a file the project never promised — the verify-kit precedent.

rules.summary: no roadmap table carries a Status column
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.emitAnchor: 'roadmap-claims: n/a (docs/roadmap.md has no table with a Status column)'
rules.notes: The kit knows the shape of its own roadmap and will not read a status out of a table that has none. Naming the missing column is what lets an adopter choose to adopt the shape.

rules.summary: a claim on origin is mentioned by no roadmap row
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.notes: GAP-017 itself: in the first post-010 field use a feature sat thirteen days with an approved spec and a gated phase while main said nothing about it. The remedy in the message is the ritual — flip the row in a MAIN-SIDE commit at claim time, never only on the branch.

rules.summary: a claim is on the roadmap and its row still reads idea
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.notes: The subtler half, and the likelier to be trusted: the feature IS on the roadmap, so a human skimming it believes the status. Worse than an absence, which at least looks like a gap.

rules.summary: every claim but the branch’s own is visible with a non-idea row
rules.law: GAP-017; feature 011; docs/sdlc/branch-strategy.md (Number Allocation)
rules.emitAnchor: roadmap-claims: OK ($checked claim(s) visible with non-idea rows
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict, and it names the exempted number. A branch is exempt for its OWN claim so a fresh claim’s first CI run cannot deadlock on a row the same change is about to flip — stating the exemption is what stops it being mistaken for coverage.

rules.summary: a claim's roadmap row names an Owner who is not on the declared developer roster
rules.law: specs/021-developer-roster FR-005; docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md
rules.notes: Graded only where a usable roster is declared (D4, D5): with none the output is byte-identical to before, which 'pass-no-roster' and 'pass-empty-roster' assert. An idea row, a blank or em-dash Owner and the checked branch's own claim are not graded, and a pass case each says so. Membership is exact, case-insensitive and trimmed (D3); it catches a stranger or a typo and does not prove identity (D9).

rules.summary: a roster is declared and a claim has no Owner column to be read from: the whole roadmap, or the table the claim is in
rules.law: specs/021-developer-roster FR-005, FR-007; plan Risks (roadmap shape)
rules.notes: The existing n/a idiom for an adopter-authored roadmap in another shape: nothing to read an Owner from, so the check says it graded neither the Owners nor the claim counts instead of passing silently. It is a line before the OK verdict, not an n/a verdict, because the visibility reading did run. Two sites, one rule: the whole roadmap has no Owner column, and (review F6) a claim whose only rows sit in a table without one while another table has one; the second also withdraws the OK line's statement that Owners were graded.

rules.summary: one Owner holds more than two active, non-stale claims
rules.law: specs/021-developer-roster FR-007; docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md (WIP limit)
rules.notes: Active is a row Status of specified or in progress; idea, shipped and dropped are not, a tip with no commit for fourteen days is not, and the checked branch's own claim is exempt as it is from visibility (D7). The count is per Owner. With no roster the count is not graded and the output is byte-identical to before (pass-no-roster).

rules.summary: one Owner holds exactly two active claims, noted and never failed
rules.law: specs/021-developer-roster FR-007; docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md (pipelining exception)
rules.notes: Two claims are lawful only under the pipelining conditions (one awaiting review, one active, territory disjoint or sequenced), which a script cannot see; so it says so and exits 0. The 'fail' direction of this rule is therefore exit 0 with the note printed, as CLAIM-010's is.

rules.summary: the tip date of a candidate claim cannot be read, so the Owner's count is UNGRADED
rules.law: specs/021-developer-roster FR-007, plan D7, D8; feature 015 (a comparison not made is never OK)
rules.notes: The line naming the Owner and the claim whose date was unreadable; the UNGRADED verdict line that replaces OK is declared a roll-up in emission-idioms.json (it also carries CLAIM-014's clause). A date is read only for an Owner with two or more candidate claims, so a corrupt tip on a lone claim reads nothing (pass-single-claim-reads-no-date). Exit 0 in both directions: UNGRADED is a verdict, never an exit code.

rules.summary: a claim is named by rows with different Owners, after preferring the rows that hold its own Spec path, so it cannot be graded
rules.law: specs/021-developer-roster FR-005, FR-007, plan D4; phase 3 review F1; feature 015 (a comparison not made is never OK)
rules.emitAnchor: named by rows with different Owners
rules.notes: A claim is bound to its row by a delimited token, preferring the row that holds specs/<claim>; a row that only mentions it, or a claim whose name is a prefix of another, does not take it (CLAIM-009 fail-prefix-claim, CLAIM-011 pass-cross-reference-not-counted). When that still leaves rows that disagree on the Owner there is nothing true to grade, so the Owner and the count are not graded and the verdict is UNGRADED, never a guess: a false failure here would fail a lawful Owner. Exit 0.

rules.summary: a claim the visibility reading found is bound to no roadmap row by the strict token, so its Owner and count cannot be graded
rules.law: specs/021-developer-roster FR-005, FR-007, plan D4; phase 3 round 2 review R2-1; feature 015 (a comparison not made is never OK)
rules.notes: The visibility reading matches a claim loosely (the name anywhere in a row) and the Owner and count readings bind it strictly (a delimited token, case-insensitive, a final full stop allowed). A claim that passes the first and matches nothing under the second used to leave the readings in silence while the OK line said Owners were graded; now the Owner is not graded, said out loud, and the verdict is UNGRADED, exit 0. The two sibling fixtures in CLAIM-009 pin the cases that must still bind: a final full stop and capitals.

rules.summary: there is no origin remote to compare claims against
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: Declines rather than printing CLEAN, which would be a claim that nothing overlaps made by a run that looked at nothing.

rules.summary: the branch shares no file with any open feature branch
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: The affirmative verdict names the branch it is about. On a team a bare CLEAN would not say whose territory was checked, which is the only part that matters.

rules.summary: the branch shares files with another open feature branch
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: Names the other branch, its staleness and every shared path: an overlap whose files you cannot see is an overlap nobody can sequence.

rules.summary: at least one overlapping claim is live
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: The kit’s whole stance on shared territory, and the reason exit 2 is advisory. A check that simply refused would push two owners into working around it.

rules.summary: every overlapping claim is stale and therefore reclaimable
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md; team-workflow rule 3
rules.notes: Exit 0, not 2: a claim nobody is working can be adopted, and blocking on it would make an abandoned branch a permanent obstacle. The pair differs only in the age of one commit.

rules.summary: the JSON contract answers when there is no remote
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: The one place this script’s machine output says less than its prose: a JSON caller cannot tell “nothing overlaps” from “nothing was checked”. Pinned as it stands and recorded as a finding — the contract belongs to feature 003, not to this phase.

rules.summary: the JSON report carries the branch, the verdict and every overlap
rules.law: docs/sdlc/team-workflow.md rule 5 (overlap is sequenced, not forbidden); feature 003 contract specs/003-flow-efficiency-pack/contracts/territory-check-cli.md
rules.notes: Built by a different code path from the prose report and carrying the same facts, which is the property worth pinning. The anchor names the ConvertTo-Json line rather than the object literal above it: the emission spans two source lines and the scanner reads one line at a time, which the anchor-ambiguity assertion reported as 0 sites rather than letting the entry measure nothing.

rules.summary: each member announces itself by name before it runs
rules.law: feature 006 contract specs/006-verification-pack/contracts/ritual-checks-ci.md; docs/sdlc/definition-of-done.md; feature 015 SC-005
rules.notes: The member names are this wrapper’s entire interface: branch protection names one required check, adopted-project docs quote these names, and SC-005 is the promise that they do not move. The pair differs by whether the tree is adopted, because that is the only thing that changes which members exist.

rules.summary: each member gets exactly one verdict line
rules.law: feature 006 contract specs/006-verification-pack/contracts/ritual-checks-ci.md; docs/sdlc/definition-of-done.md; feature 015 SC-005
rules.notes: Never short-circuits: a failing member does not stop the others, because one run must report every problem rather than the first. Three verdicts share this one site — OK, FAIL, and the member’s own n/a reason lifted out of its output.

rules.summary: the adoption doctor did not run, and the run says so rather than omitting it
rules.law: feature 006 contract specs/006-verification-pack/contracts/ritual-checks-ci.md; docs/sdlc/definition-of-done.md; feature 015 SC-005
rules.notes: The gate mirrors the doctor’s own discriminator (.kit-version OR kit-adoption.json). A silent omission would leave a reader counting six verdicts where the documentation promises seven, unable to tell a skipped check from a forgotten one — SC-004 at the wrapper level.

rules.summary: at least one member failed, and the run fails with it
rules.law: feature 006 contract specs/006-verification-pack/contracts/ritual-checks-ci.md; docs/sdlc/definition-of-done.md; feature 015 SC-005
rules.notes: The count is failing members out of members that RAN, which is what separates “one thing broke” from “the tree did”. The fail fixture puts two inert members beside the failing one: an n/a must neither mask a failure nor be counted as a pass, and the line reads 1 of 6 rather than 1 of 4.

rules.summary: every member that ran exited 0
rules.law: feature 006 contract specs/006-verification-pack/contracts/ritual-checks-ci.md; docs/sdlc/definition-of-done.md; feature 015 SC-005
rules.notes: The one line a CI badge reads. Printed once, last, and after every member’s own verdict — never instead of them. Its pass fixture is a run whose members include two inert ones, because “nothing failed” and “everything was checked” are different claims and only the first is being made.

rules.summary: the machine half of gate 5 has no diff base, so it inspects no review file and says so
rules.law: DoD gate 5; constitution I; roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: GAP-027's canonical site. This was a bare `return`: the check stopped before listing a single candidate and the run printed OK. Both directions carry the SAME review file - no provenance section, no attestation, the implementer named as reviewer - and differ only in whether the base resolves. The pass direction therefore shows the exact violation the fail direction let through, which is a stronger statement than an absence. UNGRADED, never FAIL: FR-011 forbids a new hard failure on this lane (plan D6).

rules.summary: the Lite lane's guards grade an EMPTY file list because no base resolves
rules.law: constitution X (Lite lane); roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: The one member that does not DECLINE on a null base - it grades, and grades nothing, which passes the way an empty accusation is never proved. The pack's own comment said it before this phase did: a baseless 'fix/' branch touching anything at all went green. The fixture touches a dependency manifest, a prohibited category, and the pass direction reports it. A vacuous grade reaches the same wrong verdict as a skipped one and is named the same way.

rules.summary: the Micro phase walk has no diff base, so 'exactly one phase' and the line bound compare nothing
rules.law: constitution X (Micro lane); roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: Reached through the unreadable-parent state ('truncateCommit'), which is why that fixture capability exists: a corrupt BLOB is met by a check that reads a file out of history, and a check that walks the commit graph never touches one. The fail direction also shows the combined verdict - AmendmentAuthority FAILS for want of a base while three other members report UNGRADED - which is the shape the runner prints ungraded lines independently of the verdict word to support.

rules.summary: no commit is measured against the phase-size guideline because no base resolves
rules.law: FR-006 (feature 006); constitution X; roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: The advisory member, included deliberately. A check whose only output is a WARN still has an opinion to fail to form, and leaving it out would have said that an advisory check is not worth knowing the status of - the same reasoning that pulled PhaseSizeWarning itself into the denominator in phase 3. Depth-1 clone, the ordinary actions/checkout shape.

rules.summary: a member ran and formed no opinion, and the run says so instead of OK
rules.law: feature 015 FR-009/FR-010; roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: The aggregator half of GAP-027. enforcement-pack can now report UNGRADED; this is the rule that the single entry point an adopted project runs does not print RESULT OK over the top of it. Exit 0 in BOTH directions, asserted by both cases: the verdict changes and the exit code does not, which is the whole of plan D6. Built on stub members, like every other RIT case, so it tests the aggregation and not the member.

rules.summary: every commit on the branch was skipped, so the run graded nothing and says so
rules.law: feature 015 FR-010; roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: The general case the per-site conversions do not reach. Invoke-ScopeCheck returns a skip for a merge commit, for a commit with no 'phase N' token, and for a pre-006 tree with no tasks.md; a branch made only of those exits 0 having graded nothing, and before this the wrapper printed OK. Counted the way scripts/scope-check-repos.ps1 has counted since feature 012 ($graded), so the two members answer the same question the same way. The pair differs in one commit's SUBJECT LINE - 'work: the thing' against 'phase 1: the thing' - which is the whole of the condition (plan D10).

rules.summary: a Standard phase commit whose changed files git cannot read fails the commit with an ERROR instead of passing with 0 files
rules.law: docs/sdlc/review-process.md; constitution X (territory rule); specs/032-scope-check-unreadable-commit FR-001, FR-003; roadmap GAP-038
rules.emitAnchor: its changed files could not be read
rules.notes: Added in feature 032. The fail direction truncates the commit's tree (truncateCommit HEAD^{tree}); on the parent commit it printed PASS (0 file(s)) and exit 0 for a commit it had not graded. The pass direction is SCOPE-019's fixture; pass-empty pins that a readable empty commit keeps printing PASS (0 file(s)). SCOPE-029 and SCOPE-030 share this emission site (one function prints the line).

rules.summary: a Micro phase commit whose changed files git cannot read fails the commit with an ERROR instead of passing with 0 files
rules.law: docs/sdlc/review-process.md; constitution X (territory rule); specs/032-scope-check-unreadable-commit FR-001, FR-003; roadmap GAP-038
rules.emitAnchor: its changed files could not be read
rules.notes: Added in feature 032. The Micro lane reads the changed files through the same function as the Standard lane (plan P3); the pass direction is SCOPE-016's fixture. Shares its emission site with SCOPE-028.

rules.summary: the guard that refuses a deletion or rename of tasks.md or spec.md names a commit whose changed files it cannot read instead of standing down as not applicable
rules.law: docs/sdlc/review-process.md; constitution X (territory rule); specs/032-scope-check-unreadable-commit FR-001, FR-003; roadmap GAP-038
rules.emitAnchor: its changed files could not be read
rules.notes: Added in feature 032. A commit with no phase token that deletes tasks.md and whose tree is unreadable used to print not applicable and UNGRADED (exit 0), hiding the deletion; the pass direction is the same commit readable, which the guard refuses. Shares its emission site with SCOPE-028.

rules.summary: under -All, a merge base git cannot read (git merge-base fails, as opposed to answering that there is none) fails the run with an ERROR instead of printing UNGRADED and exiting 0
rules.law: docs/sdlc/review-process.md; constitution X (territory rule); specs/034-scope-check-unchecked-reads FR-001, FR-003; roadmap GAP-040
rules.emitAnchor: could not read the merge base with main
rules.notes: Added in feature 034. The fail direction truncates the tip commit (truncateCommit HEAD): git merge-base exits 128. On the parent commit it printed UNGRADED could not resolve a merge base and exit 0, the words and exit of a branch with no shared history or no trunk. pass is SCOPE-025/pass; pass-orphan pins that a branch with no history in common (merge-base exit 1) keeps its UNGRADED text and exit 0; the missing-trunk state is pinned by SCOPE-025/fail.

rules.summary: under -All, a commit list git cannot read (git rev-list over the range fails after the merge base was read) fails the run with an ERROR instead of reading as an empty range
rules.law: docs/sdlc/review-process.md; constitution X (territory rule); specs/034-scope-check-unchecked-reads FR-001, FR-003; roadmap GAP-040
rules.emitAnchor: could not list the commits since the merge base
rules.notes: Added in feature 034. First recorded as exempt (the plan believed every damage fails git merge-base first); the phase 1 review (finding F1) showed the state is reachable: with a commit-graph written (recipe field commitGraph, feature 034), git merge-base answers from the graph while a truncated tip commit makes git rev-list exit 128. The fail direction writes the graph and then truncates the tip commit; pass is the same readable. Shares nothing with SCOPE-031, whose fail has no graph (merge-base itself fails).

rules.summary: the ungraded state is lifted for every member that can reach it, not only the first
rules.law: feature 015 FR-010; roadmap GAP-027
rules.notes: Added in the phase-5 remediation (review F1). $ungradedCapableMembers is an allow-list, so the mechanism RIT-006 proves is silently inert for any member left out of it - which is how scope-check shipped its own GAP-027 fail-open through a phase that existed to close GAP-027. This case stubs scope-check instead of enforcement-pack and asserts the same three things: the word on the member's line, the word on the RESULT line, exit 0. It fails if a future edit drops a name from that list, which RIT-006 would not notice. The anchor is the same emission site RIT-006 names, and that is deliberate rather than sloppy: the allow-list is not itself an emission site, and the site it governs is this one. RIT-006 asks whether the line can be printed at all; RIT-007 asks whether it is printed for the second member to reach the state. One site, two rules, said out loud - the inventory allows it and the ambiguity check counts hits per rule, not rules per hit.

rules.summary: the ungraded state is lifted for roadmap-claims, a member that can now reach it

rules.notes: Feature 021 teaches roadmap-claim-check.ps1 to say UNGRADED when a claim's tip date or Owner cannot be read. rules.summary: a merge commit, or a parent of one, that cannot be read is refused rather than skipped, so a merge is never passed on a wrong reason
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority; feature 026 plan D7 (a skipped merge on a wrong reason is GAP-027's shape)
rules.emitAnchor: so what the merge authored is unknown
rules.notes: Feature 026 phase 2 (plan D7). Reached with truncateCommit naming the TREE of the second parent (HEAD^2^{tree}): the commit object stays intact, so git merge-base and rev-list, which walk commits, succeed and the merge reaches the check, which refuses it. The pass is the same merge with every object readable (it authored nothing and is counted as a merge), so the twin differs only in the damaged tree. A first version of this inventory declared the rule an exemption, on the reasoning that a truncated parent COMMIT breaks merge-base first (true: measured, it ends on AMEND-004) and a shallow clone is refused by AMEND-003; the phase 2 review (F3) showed that the tree, not the commit, is the object that reaches the site. A blob that is unreadable (truncateBlob) is not this rule: the exemption helpers read it as empty and the merge is graded, fail-closed, as every ordinary commit already is.

rules.summary: a Lite-lane branch (fix/, chore/, docs/) the amendment check cannot grade is named UNGRADED and never newly failed
rules.law: feature 014 FR-009 (the Lite lane is never newly failed on a condition it cannot compute); feature 027 plan D8, spec FR-008
rules.notes: Feature 027 phase 2. ONE emission site, the Lite arm of Invoke-AmendmentAuthorityCheck: after the gate has found a spec document in the diff, each refusal the numbered lane fails on (a shallow clone, no base, an unreadable commit, tree or merge, unparsed metadata) is moved from the failures to the UNGRADED list with its own text, and the run exits 0 reading 'not graded', never clean. A failure that grades an amendment (no record, approver not in the message) is not moved. The site is the conversion, not the condition, so one site serves every refusal; the fail direction is shown for the two that a recipe can reach: fail (a clone that is shallow and still has a diff base, built with the recipe field shallowAllBranches, because a plain shallow fixture has no base and the gate stays silent) and fail-lite-unreadable-parent (the parent's copy of the script cannot be inflated, AMEND-005's damage mode). Each has a numbered-lane twin over the same state that keeps the failure: pass and pass-numbered-twin-unreadable-parent, named pass because they are the rule's other direction (the lane that keeps its refusal), and expecting exit 1. The no-base and unparsed-metadata refusals are not reachable on a Lite branch (the gate is silent without a base) or are exempted as on the numbered lane (AMEND-007), and an unreadable base tree is AMEND-010's exemption. After the phase 2 review (F3, F4) the rule gained fail-lite-unreadable-merge-parent (the merge refusal; the damage is on a side branch, because AMEND-008 puts it on main, which is the diff base, and that empties the gate's diff), fail-lite-failure-kept-beside-refusal (its twin without a record: a real amendment failure stays a failure while the refusal beside it is named UNGRADED), and a guard in Coverage.Tests.ps1, 'the Lite lane converts refusals by their text', which holds every refusal literal of the core to the conversion pattern and every grading failure out of it, because the conversion is coupled to the text of the messages.

rules.summary: the tree of the diff base cannot be read, so whether another feature's document was approved there is unknown and the check refuses
rules.law: constitution I, Amendment authority; feature 027 plan D2 (an unreadable base is never read as "nothing was approved")
rules.exemption: Needs the diff base's tree to be unreadable while every earlier read of the same range succeeds. The base is the first parent of the branch's first commit (and, in a replay, the left end of the range), so a damaged base tree breaks the commit batch (git log --name-status over the range) and the per-commit boundary read (AMEND-005) before this site is reached; for a merge, the base is one of the merge's parents, which the merge readability check (AMEND-008) refuses first, by design (the base is read only after the merge and its parents proved readable). Measured: truncateCommit naming main's tree with -IgnoreAmendmentBoundary lifts the boundary read and still ends on 'graded 2 of 2' because the name-status batch comes back empty, so a fixture would pin a different outcome under this rule's name (the defect that would then be hiding is the empty batch, which is a separate rule's concern). Exempted rather than faked.
rules.notes: Feature 027 phase 1 (plan D2, D8). Two emission sites share one failure text (the ordinary-commit row loop and the merge helper's result); the refusal is defensive and fails closed: a base that cannot be read must not be read as an empty set, which would exempt every amendment of another feature's document as a creation. The id AMEND-009 is reserved by plan D8 for the Lite lane's UNGRADED lines (phase 2).

rules.notes: Feature 028 phases 1 and 2. rules.notes: Feature 028 phases 1 and 2. ONE emission site, the Lite arm of Add-DiffUnreadable, one UNGRADED line per reader that graded nothing, exit 0, the verdict reading 'not graded', never OK. Three readers reach it: LiteAndAbuse (fix/ and chore/, phase 1), review-provenance and the Lite amendment gate (every Lite lane, phase 2); a fix/ or chore/ branch lists all three, a docs/ branch the last two. fail, fail-chore and fail-blob-rename-detection are the fix/ and chore/ lanes over the src-truncated branch and over a second damage shape (no tree is unreadable, but a blob that rename detection must read is, so git diff exits 128 the same way, and only the dispatch's rename-detecting read fails while the gate's --no-renames read succeeds: that case is what guards the gate's first-read test); fail-docs is the docs/ lane. pass is the numbered twin over the same damage (the lane that keeps its failure), named pass because it is the rule's other direction, and expecting exit 1, as AMEND-009 does. pass-lite-readable, pass-docs-readable, pass-docs-readable-review and pass-lite-empty-diff are the controls: a readable or empty diff prints exactly what it printed before (pass-docs-readable-review: a provenance-less review file is graded and failed when the diff is readable). Not guarded by a fixture, stated: a partial list (git builds the whole tree diff before it prints, so a failing diff prints nothing), the gate's second read failing alone (with --no-renames it reads no more than the dispatch's read, so it fails only when that one already has: mutations M10 and M11 are equivalent), and review-provenance's read failing alone (same trees, same rename detection).

rules.notes: Feature 029 phase 2. ONE emission site: the refusal printed once at the first failed read of the walk (Read-AmendmentGit records it; Test-AmendmentReadFailed prints it at the next boundary). The numbered lane fails; the Lite lane converts it to UNGRADED by the existing prefix rule ('AmendmentAuthority: cannot grade '). Reached by fixtures for three reads: the name-status batch (G5, a middle commit's subtree truncated by truncateCommit naming a subtree), the blob read of an amended plan.md (G7, a truncated blob, exit 255: the status-only check reads the blob before git show -U0 does; also a Lite twin, where the parent FAILED the branch with 'no conforming approver record', a new hard failure on a condition the check could not compute) and the blob read of a tick-only tasks.md (G7). Each has a readable twin. The metadata batch (G4), the range rev-list (G6), git show -U0 (G8, which only runs after the blob read that already failed), the rename same-content compare (G9) and the renumbering ls-tree (G10) have no reachable data state (they read the same objects a successful read has just read) and are guarded by injected-failure mutations recorded in notes.md, not by fixtures (plan Amendment 1).

rules.notes: Feature 029 phase 4 (G13a). The committed diff needs trees only; git diff --name-only HEAD compares content, and reads the committed blob when the working copy is stat-dirty and the same length as it (diffcore_skip_stat_unmatch), so a damaged blob fails THIS read alone and the branch's own dirty files used to drop out of the overlap check. 'fail' truncates the blob (truncateCommit naming HEAD:path: truncateBlob silently does nothing when the object is not loose) and edits the working copy to the same length; 'pass' is the readable twin (CLEAN). Reproduced only with core.autocrlf false, which the fixtures set; with autocrlf true git reads the blob in more states.
